standard_prerequisites.name: The morphism defined by a basis of global sections
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1615-1617: global generation of L^{\otimes 2} gives the morphism phi to P^n_k associated to a chosen basis s_0, ..., s_n of H^0(X, L^{\otimes 2}).

standard_prerequisites.name: Descending the closed immersion property
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1617-1621: to check that the morphism is a closed immersion one may replace k by its algebraic closure, so assume k algebraically closed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Automatic Cohen-Macaulay property of the curve
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1629-1633: X is Cohen-Macaulay, hence the invertible module L has no embedded associated points and the section s nonvanishing at all generic points is a regular section.

standard_prerequisites.name: The sibling very ampleness criterion
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1636-1637 and 1650-1652: all statements in the proof of this registered sibling hold with the chosen s, and the final generation-in-degree-1 argument for S^{(2)} is the same as in its proof.

core_obligations: Setup and field reduction (proof lines 1610-1621): choose a k-basis s_0, ..., s_n of H^0(X, L^{\otimes 2}); by assumption (1) the module L^{\otimes 2} is globally generated, giving the morphism phi_{L^{\otimes 2},(s_0,...,s_n)} : X -> P^n_k; the lemma asserts this is a closed immersion, and by the Descent lemma the check may be done after replacing k by its algebraic closure.

The regular section and the extra multiplication map (lines 1623-1643): for each generic point eta_i let V_i be the subspace of H^0(X, L) of sections vanishing at eta_i; global generation gives V_i != H^0(X, L), and since X has finitely many irreducible components and k is infinite there is s nonvanishing at all eta_i; by lemma-automatic X is Cohen-Macaulay so s is a regular section; hence all statements in the proof of the sibling criterion hold with this s; moreover global generation yields t in H^0(X, L) with t|_Z nonvanishing (finitely many points), which makes the multiplication map mu_n : H^0(X, L) \otimes_k H^0(X, L^{\otimes 2}) -> H^0(X, L^{\otimes 3}) surjective.

Generation of the section ring and conclusion (lines 1644-1654): with the exact sequence used in the sibling argument one gets S = \oplus_{n >= 0} H^0(X, L^{\otimes n}) generated in degrees 0, 1, 2 over k; arguing as in the proof of the sibling criterion, the Veronese subring S^{(2)} = \oplus_n S_{2n} is generated in degree 1, which means L^{\otimes 2} is very ample as desired; the author closes the proof with 'Some details omitted.' (recorded verbatim; see notes).
proof_roadmap: Define the morphism to projective space from a basis of H^0(L^{\otimes 2}) and reduce to k algebraically closed.
Manufacture a regular section s and, using an extra generator t, prove mu_n surjective.
Conclude that S is generated in degrees 0, 1, 2 and S^{(2)} in degree 1, hence L^{\otimes 2} is very ample.
difficulty_reason: Criterion lemma (statement 1593-1604, proof 1606-1654): under global generation, H^1 = 0 and ampleness, the square of L is very ample - the proof descends the closed immersion check to the algebraic closure, builds a regular section through the Cohen-Macaulay property, reuses the argument of the registered sibling criterion while adding the multiplication-map surjectivity obtained from global generation, and finishes by generation of the section ring in low degrees; the argument structure is complete, with the delegation and the closing 'Some details omitted.' recorded in the notes. H3: reduction-plus-reuse argument with a section-ring conclusion.
